mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls by >10% in 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 3% over three consecutive months, accompanied by a concurrent fall in real retail sales (RSAFS), signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity that depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >3% for 3 consecutive months AND RSAFS declines >2% in same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 1% for more than six months signals an extended period of monetary accommodation, which lowers borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) alongside a surge in housing starts (HOUST) signals a robust demand environment, which boosts corporate revenues and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows >0.5% month-over-month AND HOUST rises >5% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 2% for four consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of periods where INDPRO rises >2% for four consecutive months.
